habitat: Coastal and montane forest, mostly below 1 000 m, and riverine forest. Singly or in pairs in the canopy and middle layer.
summary: A common resident. Black crown and back, white stripes on the sides of the head, bold yellow edges on the folded wing, and a yellow rump in flight. Whitish below, with a yellow belly. The immature has yellow-tipped back feathers. The call is a series of poop notes. The Kemp name Goldenrumped Tinker Barbet and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Yellow-fronted Tinkerbird has a yellow forehead and pale-yellow underparts.

head.pattern: White stripes on the sides of the head.

underparts.pattern: Whitish below, with a yellow belly.

wings.pattern: Bold yellow feather edges on the folded wing.

viewNotes.note: Black crown and back, with white head stripes and yellow wing edges.
The yellow rump is visible in flight.
Whitish below, with a yellow belly.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: 'poop poop poop poop poop', usually five or six notes. No South African grade A recording was found. The grade A file is an alarm call from Uganda. The filename is XC265020-Bunyangabu-2015-03-04-10h21 LS114638.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. No South African grade A recording was found, so the Ugandan alarm call is used. The Kemp name Goldenrumped Tinker Barbet and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 16–64.
